round3_error_analysis.root_cause: round3_b591_b592_final.py computed d_max against a POOL of 1,009,679 maximum sets found by local search, not against the true family M_8. Its json field 'complete: true' means the branch-and-bound over the pool ran to completion, NOT that the pool equals M_8. The pool is a strict subset, so the reported max-overlap (hence d_max) was a LOWER bound, reported as exact.
round3_error_analysis.corroboration: round3's own text already flagged 'pool_ub' as an upper bound on d_max, and the n=6 K=11 record is exactly reproducible by the correct method (464 maximal sets), showing the method is right at n<=7 where M_n is enumerable.

notes.K9: K_9 >= 17 is known (PROTOCOL.md, cert terminal) but the exact value is NOT established, so the 'one stone short' layer size for n=9 is undefined
notes.layer_enumeration: n=8 14-stone layer has C(64,14) ~ 2.1e11 members; n=9 16-stone layer has C(81,16) ~ 1.1e17. Neither is enumerable, so d_max for those layers can only ever be a per-SET exact value, never a layer maximum.
notes.bug_found_and_fixed_during_round4: the first version of greedy_alpha() returned popc(S&M) for a set M of size < K, which is not in the domain of alpha (which is max over |M| = K). This produced alpha = |S|, hence d_max = 0, for any S that no maximum set contains. Detected because the known n=7 worst set came out 0 instead of 8. Fixed: greedy_alpha now only returns the overlap of a safe set of size exactly K, and falls back to 0.
